correctness.rationale: Poisson thinning transforms the exact sequential race into independent Gamma(shape k, rate k) finish times. The two last-place probabilities are obtained by explicit Laplace transforms and a finite Erlang-density integral; both independent integral expansions were cross-checked for integer n=2..32. Their algebraic differences are exact rational functions of n and r_c=(n/(n+c))^n. A reproducible exact-Fraction program checked each of 498 n in [2,499], including both gaps and the n=2 tie. For n>=500, log(1+u) bounds and rational series bounds for e provide two proved lower margins: 20931734927/2484922590000>1/200 and 114949/10353000>1/100. These cover all integers beyond the finite range. No finite enumeration was used as evidence of the unbounded case.

value.rationale: The 2026 lead paper explicitly shows that three-way last-place ordering is subtle and globally nonmonotone, with an observed middle-player never-maximal pattern but no general rule. The goals (1,2,n) are the first strictly unequal three-player family with a free integer parameter, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. A complete infinite-family ranking, precise n=2 tie, and nonvanishing uniform gaps for every n>=3 answer a natural structural question about these Poisson/Erlang competitions. The exact inequalities are stronger than computing another isolated instance, while not purporting to solve the full arbitrary-goal comparison problem.
